column3: Close to the Greek; “family” is rendered “lineage.”
NKJV has “his betrothed wife,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “who was betrothed to him.”
Close to the Greek; “place” is rendered “room.”
NKJV begins with “behold,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV has “goodwill toward men,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “among men of (His) good pleasure.”
NKJV has “the shepherds,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “the shepherds were saying,” without the extra “the men.”
NKJV has “made widely known,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “made known.”
NKJV has “the Child,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “to circumcise Him.”
NKJV has “her purification”; the Greek reads “their purification.”
Close to the Greek; “righteous” is rendered “just.”
Close to the Greek; “Master” (δεσπότης) is rendered “Lord.”
